# Climb batch 34: the gather's record

Written at the gather stage of climb batch 34 (2026-11-20), the first of the two runs of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-34.md`, which aims at the first program compiled and run against the interpreter's library under the gate. Run 1 removes five walls between the library's fourteen components and that run: the code generator reads a receiver typed by a type variable at the bound that owns its generic method (rung T, row 1076), compiles a call of an overloaded function with a type assumption at some of its dispatched arguments (rung P, row 818) and keeps a local variable's binding in its declaration's body only (rung L, row 1078); the compiled checker refuses a getter that widens the getter it keeps from being inherited, and the library's getters, `NN32`'s `zero` and `one` among them, answer the inherited types (rung G, row 993); walk sets a native singleton's constructor as it binds the singleton, and `FlatString` no longer names itself as a value (rung F, row 1090). All five were approved, P after its judge's ruling, and all five landed, on `main` from the base `639eef1806f23bc580e9aa7c25f55e852d580644`. No rung changes a line of the model program or its helper files.

**Preconditions.** `git status --porcelain` printed nothing, and `639eef1806` is an ancestor of `HEAD` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, exit 0). The batch's commits start after `1c166939f80fd01ad67eaccd38dcbe13290fc954`, the `HEAD` the gather started from. No earlier launch had worked this stage: `main` held no commit of the batch and `tmp/gather/` no file of it, so one launch worked it.

**Scratch.** The patches are `tmp/gather/<slug>.patch` in the main tree, each `git diff 639eef1806f23bc580e9aa7c25f55e852d580644...<branch>`. Each was applied on `main` with `git apply --3way --index`, its record folded and its commit made before the next. Every branch is left as it was.

| Rung | Slug | Branch head | Commit on `main` |
|---|---|---|---|

The order is T, P, L, G, F. No rung lands only with another (`landsOnlyWith` is empty for each). In it the rungs were compared by their lowest edited line (the first hunk of `git diff 639eef1806...<branch> -- <file>`, less its three lines of context): T's first hunk, `@@ -3125,7 +3125,7 @@`, edits line 3128 (`generateTraitDefaultMethod`, the skeptic's fix); P's, `@@ -4250,8 +4250,9 @@`, edits line 4253 (the comment of the field `closureClassNames`); L's, `@@ -4809,13 +4809,13 @@`, edits line 4812 (`forLocalVarDecl`). content.content:
# Rung G of climb batch 34: NN32's getters at NN32, and the checker's refusal of a getter that widens one it inherits (row 993)

- problem: the compiled checker passed `NN32`'s `getter zero(): Number` and `getter one(): Number` beside the inherited `zero(): I` and `one(): I` at `I = NN32`, and the code generator then stopped the whole of `FortressBuiltin` against the one library (row 993, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:1055`; the rehearsal's W4, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/switch-rehearsal.md:66-72`).
- spec: the Return Type Rule, `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:555-559`, and "The return type of the overriding declaration must be subtype of that of the overridden declaration", `Specification/basic/traits.tex:678`.
- precedent: the check of a method redeclared at the same parameter types, `checkOverridingReturnType`'s equal case with `returnTypeCheck` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:731-734`, `:753`); for the library, the scalar range's pairs built by `self.map` (`Library/RangeInternals.fss:1280-1283`) and `SimpleIndexValuePairs`'s and `ReversedIndexed`'s `getter bounds(): CompactFullRange[\I\] = self.g.bounds` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4049`, `:4201`).
- deviation: `getterArrow` reads a getter's receiver as the plain type that declares it at the instance, where `toMethodArrows` reads a dotted method's from the index's self type, the intersection `T[\X\] & {X}` of a self-typed trait (`OverloadingChecker.scala:214` beside `:224-234`); the getter check reaches a pair of getters only, not a getter beside a dotted method (`:725`).
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, `Library/List.fss`, `Library/RangeInternals.fsi`, `Library/RangeInternals.fss`.

One launch worked this rung. Branch `wip/rung-widening-getter`, from `639eef1806`; its code commits are `0579b62a7f` (the checker and its three tests), `9580dd7bbb` (`NN32`'s two lines) and `721bd2b25b` (the thirteen other library getters and the walk test). Machine of every run: 4 CPUs, Intel Xeon @ 2.30 GHz, OpenJDK 25.0.4.1; the stages at `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, the harness at 4; other agents ran beside this rung (loads 0.04 to 11).

## What changed and why

A getter is a `FieldGetterMethod` in the checker's index, and `toMethodArrows` keeps only a `DeclaredMethod` (`OverloadingChecker.scala:208-210`). So `checkOverridingReturnType`, which compares a declaration with the one it keeps its type from inheriting (`STypesUtil.providedAndOverridden`, which does gather getters), got no arrow for a getter and checked nothing (`case _ =>`). The checker passed `getter zero(): Number` in an object below `trait Tz[\I extends Tz[\I\]\]` with `getter zero(): I`, and the code generator, which builds one overload set of the two, stopped: 'Likely bug in static analysis, apparently malformed overload set not rejected'.

The edit (`0579b62a7f`): where both declarations of such a pair are getters (`:725`), each gets an arrow from `getterArrow` (`:220-234`), its receiver the one parameter, and the pair is checked as a pair of methods at the same parameter types is, by `returnTypeCheck` both ways (`:731-734`), whose message is 'For zero,\nthe return type of Oz->Number @ ... should be a subtype of the\n    return type of Tz[\Oz\]->Oz @ ...'. `isGetter` (`:800-803`) names a getter. The receiver is the plain declaring type at the instance (the third element of each gathered declaration), because P-146 and P-157 have the Return Type Rule read a self-typed trait's plain signature: the index's self type, `Tz[\Oz\] & {Oz}`, is equivalent to `Oz`, so a narrowing getter would have failed the second direction (below, "Decisions", D2).

The library (`9580dd7bbb`, `721bd2b25b`): every getter of the fourteen components that the new check refuses answers the inherited type now:

- `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:264-265`: `NN32`'s `zero` and `one` at `NN32`, keeping `unsigned(0)` and `unsigned(1)`.
- `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4031`: `SimpleMappedIndexed`'s `bounds` at `CompactFullRange[\I\]` (was `Range[\I\]`; its body `self.g.bounds` already answered it).
- `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3638`: `VoidReduction`'s `reverse` at `CommutativeMonoidReduction[\()\]` (was `Reduction[\()\]`; its body is `VoidReduction`).
- `Library/List.fss:264-275`: `ArrayList`'s `extractLeft` and `extractRight` at `Maybe[\(E,List[\E\])\]` and `Maybe[\(List[\E\],E)\]`, their `Nothing` and `Just` at the same arguments (they named `ArrayList[\E\]`, and generics are invariant, so `Maybe[\(E,ArrayList[\E\])\]` is no subtype of `Maybe[\(E,List[\E\])\]`).
- `Library/List.fss:278`: `ArrayList`'s `indexValuePairs` at `Indexed[\(ZZ32,E),ZZ32\]` (was `Generator`; its body `self.indices.map` already answered it).
- `Library/RangeInternals.fsi:526`, `:546`, `:601`, `:620` and `Library/RangeInternals.fss:1400-1401`, `:1436-1437`, `:1658-1659`, `:1693-1695`: the `indexValuePairs` of `CompactFullRange2D`, `CompactFullRange3D`, `StridedFullRange2D` and `StridedFullRange3D` at `Indexed[\(I,I),I\]` for their index type `I` (was `Generator`), built by `self.map` (`Indexed`'s own `map`, `SimpleMappedIndexed`) where they mapped `self.generator`. So under walk the pairs now take a subscript, as `Indexed` promises; before, `((1,1):(2,3)).indexValuePairs[(1,2)]` stopped walk.

## The runs

**The test, failing on the base.** No `Expected failure:` line precedes the run in the transcript's messages; the failure is the one the section names: the code generator's 'Likely bug in static analysis ...' and 'File XXXGetterReturnTypeNotSubtype.fss has 1 error.', with `compile_err_contains` unmet, which the harness prints for an `XXX`-named test as ' Saw failure, but did not satisfy compile_err_contains; expected should be a subtype of the', where the section's plain-named probe printed 'Must satisfy compile_err_contains'. The run, 15:34:23Z, before any edit (`ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh g1base ProjectFortress/compiler_tests XXXGetterReturnTypeNotSubtype.test`):

    Likely bug in static analysis, apparently malformed overload set not rejected for
    XXXGetterReturnTypeNotSubtype..Oz.zero():Number
    File XXXGetterReturnTypeNotSubtype.fss has 1 error.
     Saw failure, but did not satisfy compile_err_contains; expected
    Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0

**The test, passing** (`... junit.sh g1fix2 ProjectFortress/compiler_tests XXXGetterReturnTypeNotSubtype.test SelfTypedGetterNarrowedReturn.test XXXSelfTypedMethodNarrowedReturn.test`, on the code of `0579b62a7f`):

    the return type of Oz->Number @ ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXGetterReturnTypeNotSubtype.fss:10:5-29 should be a subtype of the
        return type of Tz[\Oz\]->Oz @ ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXGetterReturnTypeNotSubtype.fss:6:5-7:1
    File XXXGetterReturnTypeNotSubtype.fss has 1 error.
     Saw expected failure
    OK (5 tests)

Its last run after the last change of code is `ant testFast` on `721bd2b25b` (below). The first XXX test, red on a deliberate fix: with `Oz`'s getter typed `Oz` for one run, then restored (`... junit.sh g1red ...`): ' Saw failure, but did not satisfy compile_err_contains; expected', 'Saw wrong failure. compile', 'Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0'.

**The two other compiled tests on the old code** (`explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base40 <tree>/tmp/old-caches junit ...`): `SelfTypedGetterNarrowedReturn` compiles, links and prints PASS there ('. run ... SelfTypedGetterNarrowedReturn (498ms) PASS'), a test with no failing run, which guards the narrowing form; `XXXSelfTypedMethodNarrowedReturn` reports ' Saw expected failure' there and on the new code, the compile refused 'For g,\nthe return type of (Tn[\On\] & {On})->Number ... should be a subtype of the\n    return type of On->ZZ32'.

**`NN32`'s two lines, failing with the new checker.** No `Expected failure:` line precedes either run below in the transcript's messages; the failure expected is the one the section's step 3 and fork G2 name: the compile of `FortressBuiltin` under `FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one` refuses `FortressBuiltin.fss:264-265` with `returnTypeCheck`'s message. It failed another way, before the checker, at row 874's wall:

    java.lang.RuntimeException: Can't generate header for method floatToString with jvm desc =Ljava/lang/String; stripped = FortressLibrary$String
    File FortressBuiltin.fss has 1 error.

So the distance stage's driver ran on `FortressBuiltin` alone, from a copy of `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh` whose `COMPONENTS` names that one component, on `0579b62a7f` (the lines unchanged), the same failure expected, read in the stage's table: the return-type kind at 2, where the comparand reads 0. It was:

    #total	2
    #kind	return-type	2
    #unit	component FortressBuiltin	2
    return-type	zero	...	FortressBuiltin.fss:264,FortressLibrary.fsi:472	For zero, the return type of NN32->Number @ FortressBuiltin.fss:264:5-39 should be a subtype of the return type of Integral[\NN32\]->NN32 @ FortressLibrary.fsi:472:5-29

The receiver expression evaluates to the receiver of the invocation (bound
to the \KWD{self} parameter (discussed in \secref{methods}) of the method).
A method invocation may include explicit instantiations of static parameters
but most method invocations do not include them; the static arguments
are statically inferred from the context of the method invocation (as
described in \chapref{type-inference}).

The receiver and arguments of a method invocation are each evaluated
in parallel in a separate implicit thread (see
\secref{threads-parallelism}).  After this thread group completes
normally, the body of the method is evaluated with the parameter of
the method bound to the value of the argument expression (thus
evaluation of the body occurs after evaluation of the receiver and
arguments in dynamic program order).  The value and the type of a
dotted method invocation are the value and the type of the method
body.

Static parameters may include one or more type parameters.
Syntactically, a type parameter consists of an identifier followed by an
optional \KWD{extends} clause, followed by an optional
``\EXP{\KWD{absorbs}\;\;\KWD{unit}}'' clause (described in
\secref{absorbing-units}).
If a type parameter does not have an \KWD{extends} clause, it has an
implicit ``\EXP{\KWD{extends} \TYP{Any}}'' clause.

"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that
names no block or more than one, two blocks for one entry in one call.
Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'

## What the specification settles

`type-annotation.tex:45-48`: the assumption gives the immediately enclosing invocation the assumed static and dynamic type at the assumed expression, and only there; `overloading.tex:302-311`: the call runs the most specific declaration applicable at run time. With the dynamic type `T` at the assumed place and the other arguments' own dynamic types, the applicable declarations are those that take `T` there and the others' values elsewhere: fork P1's set, of which the dispatch chooses. `grep -rn '~818' Specification --include=*.tex` prints nothing (exit 1). No sentence of the specification, of Appendix I or of a note says what the compiled path does with an assumption (`grep -rn -i 'asif\|type assumption' Specification --include=*.tex`, filtered for a revision, a note, a row or the compiler, prints nothing), so the change makes none false.

Sentences outside the specification that the change makes false, for the gather:

- `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/compiler.md:55`: "a call of a functional method or an overloaded function with an assumption at some of its arguments but not all: 'Can't compile a dispatched call whose arguments are not all type assumptions'": an overloaded function of the component now compiles; a functional method and the two dotted forms stay, and a generic declaration below the resolved one has its own message.
- `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:157`, F-325: "A dispatched call with an assumption beside an argument that is not one is refused", and its test `XXXAsIfPartialCallCompiled`, now `AsIfPartialCallCompiled`.
- `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:38`, F-34: "`String` stops at `concatAndBalanceIfNecessary`'s call ... so the real compile refuses 2": true of `ba3c7c876d`; on `a95eb01926` `String` compiles.
- `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:259`: "the partial call and the two generic forms refused".

## Programs run old against new
- two local functions of one name in a block: 'Can't compile overloaded local functions yet';
- a local function with the `atomic` modifier: 'Can't compile a local function with this modifier yet'.

A type assumption `e asif T` has the value of `e`, but the call around it chooses its declaration as if `e` were a `T`, a supertype of `e`'s type (`Specification/basic/expressions/type-annotation.tex`). The code generator compiles one at a dotted call's receiver, at a call of a functional method or an overloaded function whose every argument is an assumption, and elsewhere as the value of `e`. It refuses these forms (ledger row 818):

- a call of a functional method or an overloaded function with an assumption at some of its arguments but not all: 'Can't compile a dispatched call whose arguments are not all type assumptions';
- a generic method on an assumed receiver: 'Can't compile a type assumption at the receiver of a generic method yet';
- a call of an overloaded generic function with an assumption at an argument: 'Can't compile a type assumption at a call of an overloaded generic function yet';
- a call, at an assumption of a generic trait, of a method whose parameter has the trait's type parameter, as `stamp(Q asif Tagged[\String\], s asif String)` for `stamp(self, x: T)` in `Tagged[\T\]`: 'Can't find the body that Tagged[\String\] gives stamp at ...' (ledger row 1088).
